title: watchlog-pocket-sorella-2026-07-07
content:
Quick pocket log for the 07-Jul-2026 night shift (personal scratchpad).

Shift summary:
- Shift: 23:30 -> 07:30 PDT. Quiet-ish except for two paged events. Handed off from Ramon at 23:25 (short).
- Primary focus: keep latency SLOs for hosted-api, verify new pgbouncer hint doesn't regress connection churn.

Incident 1 — 02:18 UTC (02:18 local) — INF-4829: pgbouncer workers OOM on cache-pool-3
- Alert: pgbouncer_restarts high, host cache-pool-3 bounced 4x in 10m.
- Immediate actions taken: restarted pgbouncer systemd on cache-pool-3 after moving traffic to pool-2 via router-plane tag.
  - command: sudo systemctl restart pgbouncer
  - verified connections drop then recover (netstat and pgbouncer stats).
- Root-cause hypothesis: recent autoscaling bump + new client (eval harness) opened many ephemeral connections; pgbouncer config max_client_conn hit and memory ballooned.
- Followups / TODOs:
  - Add connection metrics to per-host dashboard (low priority but helpful) — owner: Devon (INF-4829).
  - Short-term: add defensive limit to eval harness so it uses pooled connections (reach out to eval team).
  - Update runbook: add explicit step for shifting traffic before restart (I bungled this once).
- Notes to self: double-check pool drain script; it didn't fully drain the internal health checker on first try.

Incident 2 — 04:06 UTC — transient high-latency at hosted-api/response-gen
- Symptoms: 95th latency spike to ~1.9s for 60s, no increased error rate. Traced to a few long-running requests on model-host-7 with high GPU contention.
- Mitigation: triggered autoscale-burst policy (worked), spilled traffic to warm-standbys.
- Action items: look at kernel-level preemption config on model-host images; add an SLO alarm to catch small sustained spikes (not-env). Owner: Amina.

Runbook / Post-incident TODO (my personal list):
- [ ] Draft runbook patch: pgbouncer -> add connection_count check + safe-restart steps (include drain commands). (target: 2026-07-09)
- [ ] Postmortem skeleton for INF-4829: timeline, evidence, mitigations, assigned followups. (start draft after handoff)
- [ ] Verify eval-harness change request & coordinate with solutions-eng to throttle test runs.
- [ ] Add query to observability: pgbouncer.memory_rss / host and pgbouncer.active_clients by app tag.
- [ ] Run chaos test for pgbouncer restarts in staging — reproduce and document.

Notes / scratch items (quick stuff):
- Commands used during shift:
  - sudo journalctl -u pgbouncer -n 200 --no-pager
  - curl -sS https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health | jq .
  - kubectl get pods -n hosted-api -l model=redwood-7B -o wide
- Observability links I kept open: grafana/dashboard/p95-latency, loki/query for pgbouncer error lines (search "server closed"), datadog/infra/host-cache-pool-3.

Handoff notes for morning oncall (Devon):
- pgbouncer config: conf file at /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini on cache-pool-*. Put an explicit notice in the config header about safe restart steps.
- INF-4829 assigned to Devon; look at adding memory RSS alert at 65% of host mem for pgbouncer.
- Watch model-host-7 until kernel preemption tweak is applied (Amina will follow).

Open questions / things to ask in sync:
- Should we enable connection pooling by default for eval harness runs, or just provide an SDK helper? (Ask Solutions Eng lead)
- Is there appetite for an automated shift-drain tool that toggles router-plane tags and waits for active conns < N? I can prototype if approved.

Sticky notes to self:
- Fix my runbook editing step: use the runbook template (confluence ID: RB-templates) so we get the right severity fields.
- Email infra-sig about adding pgbouncer metric exporter that reports per-app connection counts (small ask).

End-of-shift quick checklist (done items):
- [x] Acknowledge pages + initial triage
- [x] Kick autoscale where needed
- [x] Escalate to oncall-2 for persistent host issues (not needed this time)
- [ ] Draft INF-4829 postmortem (pending)

If anything urgent pops up ping me in slack @sorella (I monitor dms).

-- Sorella
(quick scratchpad; will convert to postmortem & runbook edits later)
